samples.summary: The `readOnly` dependency added to the docs editor effect can never actually fire on the only route that sets `readOnly`: the share link is resolved once and never re-checked, so a revoked/downgraded link keeps a fully writable editor for the tab's lifetime.
samples.evidence:
The diff adds `readOnly` to the deps of the editor-mount effect (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:581) and justifies it as closing a real hole: "a session that *loses* write authority while open (a share link re-resolving from `editor` to `viewer`) kept a fully writable editor over a document it may no longer write."

But nothing re-resolves. `SharedDocumentByToken` calls `resolveShareLink(token)` inside a `useEffect` keyed only on `token`, stores the answer in `useState` (shared-document.tsx:1082, 1086-1102) and never refetches, polls, or invalidates it — it is not a react-query subscription. `SharedDocsLayout` then derives `const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` (shared-document.tsx:322) from that frozen value, and this is the only `DocsView` mount that passes `readOnly` at all (the owner route, packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-detail.tsx:280-300, passes none).

Attack: an owner shares an editor link, the visitor opens it, the owner then revokes the link or downgrades it to `viewer`. The visitor's tab never re-resolves, `readOnly` stays `false`, the new dep never changes, and the editor keeps writing to the Yorkie document. With `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` defaulting to `false` (shadow mode — packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:185, packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:101, and the comment at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4435-4439 says so explicitly: "in a stock deployment this is the write boundary for a viewer share token"), the stale client flag is the only write boundary, so the writes land.

The added dep is correct and harmless, but it reads as covered while the trigger it depends on does not exist. The missing half is a periodic/`onFocus` re-resolve (or a react-query subscription) for `ResolvedShareLink`.
searchedFor: Grep 'DocsView' across packages/frontend/src to enumerate every mount site
Read docs-detail.tsx:100-300 to confirm the owner route passes no readOnly
Grep 'YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE' repo-wide to confirm shadow-mode default

samples.summary: `readOnly` is computed with a deny-list comparison (`role === "viewer"`) over an untyped `role: string`, so any unrecognized role value fails OPEN into a fully writable editor.
samples.evidence:
`ResolvedShareLink.role` is declared `role: string` with no union (packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.ts:17), and every consumer writes `const readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` (shared-document.tsx:181, 322, 375, 425, 452, 740). Anything that is not the exact literal `"viewer"` — an empty string, a missing field deserialized as `undefined`, a future role such as `commenter`, or a casing/typo drift on the server — yields `readOnly === false`, which mounts the editor with the raw (unwrapped) store and no `MUTATING_METHODS` neutering (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1075, 4448). Because `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` defaults to shadow mode, that is a write boundary failing open.

This is the flag the diff makes load-bearing (docs-view.tsx:572-581 calls it "the only place that permission is applied"), so its derivation is in scope. Mitigating fact, hence the low confidence: `ShareLinkService` currently rejects any role other than `'viewer'`/`'editor'` at creation time (packages/backend/src/share-link/share-link.service.ts:79), so no third value should reach the client today. The safe form is an allowlist — `const readOnly = resolved.role !== "editor"` — which fails closed instead.
searchedFor: Read packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1062-1105 and :4430-4470 for what readOnly gates

samples.summary: The new `readOnly` re-check in `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` cannot observe a permission change — `this.readOnly` is immutable after construction — yet its comment claims it enforces the live permission at write time.
samples.evidence:
The diff adds `if (this.disposed || this.pasting || this.readOnly) return;` with a comment asserting `readOnly` "is read here, at the moment of the write, so the permission this session is allowed to exercise is the one that decides — not the one that held when the shortcut was pressed and the clipboard prompt went up."

No code supports that. `private readOnly = false` (text-editor.ts:191) is assigned exactly once, in the constructor (text-editor.ts:719), and a repo-wide grep for `setReadOnly|readOnly =` across packages/docs/src finds no other writer. A permission change tears the whole editor down and builds a new one (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:565, 581), so the *disposed* check is what actually covers that case; the `readOnly` half re-reads the identical value the keydown gate at text-editor.ts:1096-1112 already enforced (Cmd+Shift+V returns there under readOnly before ever reaching this method).

The guard itself is a harmless belt-and-braces addition. The risk is the comment: it documents a dynamic authorization re-check that does not exist, which is exactly the kind of note that makes a later reviewer stop looking for the real one (see the separate finding on share-link re-resolution). Either add a `setReadOnly()` that this can meaningfully read, or reword to "defence in depth; `readOnly` is fixed for the editor's lifetime."
searchedFor: Read text-editor.ts:6068-6094 (dispose) to confirm the disposed flag is armed on teardown

samples.summary: Inside the same effect the diff re-keys on `readOnly`, `store.setDocument(pending)` writes the whole document through the RAW store with no `readOnly` gate — unlike the `ensureTree` write two lines above it, which is gated.
samples.evidence:
Line 356 builds `const store = new YorkieDocStore(doc)` — the raw store, never wrapped in `readOnlyDocStore` (that wrapping happens only inside `initialize()`, packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1075). Line 354 correctly gates the other pre-editor write (`if (!readOnly && !ensureTree(doc)) return;`), but lines 384-401 then call `store.setDocument(pending)` on any staged DOCX import with no `readOnly` check at all, and `setDocument` is a full `writeFullDocument` that replaces the entire Yorkie tree. In shadow mode (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=false`) nothing server-side stops it, so a viewer-role mount reaching this line would overwrite the shared document just by opening it.

Why low confidence: the only mount that sets `readOnly` is `SharedDocsLayout`, and it does not pass `documentId` (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:362-368), so `if (documentId)` is false and the block is unreachable today; I also could not find any caller of `setPendingImport` for docs, so the map may never be populated. But the diff's own comment on line 572-579 asserts this effect is "the only place that permission is applied," and this write sits inside it outside that application — a later route that passes both `readOnly` and `documentId` turns it into a live viewer-write. Gate it (`if (!readOnly && documentId)`) so the property holds by construction.
searchedFor: Read shared-document.tsx:336-372 to check whether documentId is passed on the readOnly mount
Read packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts to confirm the raw store is unwrapped here

Read docs-detail.tsx:100-300 to confirm the owner route passes no readOnly
Grep 'YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE' repo-wide to confirm shadow-mode default

verdict.reason: The absence is real. `resolveShareLink` has a single call site in the entire frontend (shared-document.tsx:1093), inside a useEffect keyed only on [token] with the result parked in useState (:1082); there is no react-query subscription, no refetchInterval/refetchOnWindowFocus, no visibilitychange or setInterval touching share links anywhere in packages/frontend/src (the only such hooks are notifications, document lists and view analytics). SharedDocsLayout freezes `readOnly = resolved.role === "viewer"` (:322) from that value and hands it to DocsView (:364), so a revoked/downgraded link never changes the flag for the tab's lifetime. I also chased the indirect paths: the only other token consumer is authTokenInjector -> fetchYorkieShareToken (shared-document.tsx:746, :1000; api/auth.ts:187-205), and that endpoint performs no link validation, merely wrapping the share token in a JWT (auth.controller.ts:82-90, auth.service.ts:75-80). The server-side webhook would be the counterexample — it re-resolves the link per RPC and requires role==='editor' for writes (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:213-217) — but it ships neutered: enforce is only true when YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE==='true' (:100-101) and shadow mode converts every deny (including 401) into an allow (:111-119). The repo itself documents that default as making the client flag the write boundary (packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:39-42, packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4435-4439), and template publishing refuses to run without enforcement (template-review.ts:77-83). This is in the authorization lane: revocation/downgrade of a share credential does not take effect for an already-open session, and in the stock configuration nothing else blocks the writes.

verdict.reason: The deny-list expression exists exactly as quoted (shared-document.tsx:181,322,375,425,452,740 over `role: string` at share-links.ts:17), but its fail-open branch is unreachable and confers no attacker capability. The client's only source of `role` is `resolveShareLink()` (share-links.ts:99-111), served by the resolve endpoint that echoes `link.role` from the DB (share-link.controller.ts:67-76). The sole production writer of that column allowlists the value first — `SHARE_LINK_ROLES = ['viewer','editor']` with a BadRequestException otherwise (share-link.service.ts:11,77-81) — and a repo-wide grep for `shareLink.create|update|upsert` finds only that one call site (share-link.service.ts:92) besides tests. The "field missing/undefined" variant is closed too: the column is non-nullable with a fail-closed default `@default("viewer")` (schema.prisma:150). Most decisively, because `"editor"` is itself an accepted writable value, any actor able to influence `role` (forged response, tampered row) would simply send `"editor"` and obtain the identical writable editor under the proposed allowlist `role !== "editor"`; there is no attacker-controlled input for which the two forms differ. What remains is future-drift hardening (a later `commenter` role or server-side casing typo), i.e. minor-grade defense-in-depth, not an authorization bypass blocking under the Security rubric.

verdict.reason:
The cited code does exist as described (docs-view.tsx:384-401 calls store.setDocument on the raw store with no readOnly gate, unlike the gated ensureTree write at line 354), but the write is unreachable on two independent, verified axes, so it is not an exploitable authorization gap.

Axis A — no mount supplies both props. DocsView has exactly two production mounts: docs-detail.tsx:280-301 passes documentId but never passes readOnly (a grep of that whole file for `readOnly` returns zero hits), and shared-document.tsx:362-368 — the only surface that ever sets readOnly, derived from `resolved.role === "viewer"` at line 322 — passes no documentId. So `if (documentId)` at line 384 is false on the only viewer-capable surface.

Axis B — the registry has no producer. setPendingImport at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/pending-imports.ts:22 has zero callers in packages/frontend/src; a repo-wide grep finds only the definition, the two peek/clear consumers, and archived planning docs. apply-imported-content.ts:143-154 documents that the stash-and-apply-on-mount model was deliberately replaced by a headless applyImportedContent (live callers: upload-queue.ts:13,236 and miro-import-runner.ts:11,78), so peekPendingImport returns undefined on every mount and the try block never executes.

Completing the attack chain would require two separate future code changes (a new route passing both readOnly and documentId, plus a resurrected producer). Under the Security rubric this is a defense-in-depth/hardening suggestion, not a reachable auth bypass, and it does not weaken any currently enforced path.
